task: B.2-03A — Valcendre modular architecture and ground proof

palette.policy: every opaque pixel is an exact approved palette hex; no new colours introduced

light_direction: upper-left / northwest; cast shadow falls south and east
status: PROOF — additive. Does NOT replace public/assets/environments/valcendre_tiles_16x16.png and makes no claim on its 48 indexed slots. Remapping and integration belong to the coding agent.

alpha.rule: binary only — alpha is 0 or 255, never between

assets_containing_transparency.valcendre_proof_architecture_16x16.png: only the three structural_shadow overlay tiles (indices 13, 14, 15) contain alpha-0 pixels; all 29 other tiles are fully opaque

tiles.name: cobble_0
tiles.connection: all four variants are freely interchangeable in any orientation of neighbour; no joint pixel lands on a tile boundary, so there is no 16px lattice

tiles.name: cobble_1
tiles.connection: all four variants are freely interchangeable in any orientation of neighbour; no joint pixel lands on a tile boundary, so there is no 16px lattice

tiles.name: cobble_2
tiles.connection: all four variants are freely interchangeable in any orientation of neighbour; no joint pixel lands on a tile boundary, so there is no 16px lattice

tiles.name: cobble_3
tiles.connection: all four variants are freely interchangeable in any orientation of neighbour; no joint pixel lands on a tile boundary, so there is no 16px lattice

files.notes: coursed pavé. Horizontal joints at y2, y8, y13 give 6,5,5 spacing when stacked and never a joint on the 16px boundary. One wrap course is identical in all four variants, which is what makes them interchangeable.

files.layer: architecture, except indices 13-15 which are overlays

tiles.name: wall_limestone_a
tiles.connection: fill. Tiles freely with wall_limestone_b; the two carry opposite bonds so neighbours never repeat. Joint rows at y0 and y8 align on every masonry tile.

tiles.name: wall_limestone_b
tiles.connection: fill. Alternate bond for wall_limestone_a.

tiles.name: wall_plaster
tiles.connection: fill. Quiet facade surface; no horizontal line of its own except a 2px worn band at y14-15.

tiles.name: wall_plaster_course
tiles.connection: place as the TOP row of a 2-row facade; carries the single course line at y0-1.

tiles.name: wall_edge_top
tiles.connection: top row of a wall run with no roof above it.

tiles.name: wall_edge_bottom
tiles.connection: bottom row of a wall run meeting the ground.

tiles.name: wall_edge_left
tiles.connection: west end of a wall run. Lit return face in column 0-1.

tiles.name: wall_edge_right
tiles.connection: east end of a wall run. 1px recess at column 14, shaded return at 15.

tiles.name: wall_corner_tl
tiles.connection: north-west outside corner. Carries both the lit return and the cap.

tiles.name: wall_corner_tr
tiles.connection: north-east outside corner. Cap plus shaded return.

tiles.name: wall_corner_bl
tiles.connection: south-west outside corner. Lit return plus footing.

tiles.name: wall_corner_br
tiles.connection: south-east outside corner. Shaded return plus footing.

tiles.name: wall_plinth
tiles.connection: bottom row of a building, between facade and paving.

tiles.name: shade_footing
tiles.connection: OVERLAY on the paving row immediately south of a wall. Offset it 2-4px east for the north-west light.

tiles.name: shade_under_eave
tiles.connection: OVERLAY on the facade row immediately below an eave.

tiles.name: shade_corner
tiles.connection: OVERLAY on the paving column immediately east of a building.

tiles.name: roof_slate_a
tiles.connection: roof plane fill. Alternate with roof_slate_b to break the 16px period.

tiles.name: roof_slate_b
tiles.connection: roof plane fill, opposite bond, carries two sparse glints.

tiles.name: roof_ridge
tiles.connection: top row of a roof. Lit cap at y0-1.

tiles.name: roof_eave
tiles.connection: bottom row of a roof. 3px fascia at y11-14 and a recessed underside at y15.

tiles.name: roof_edge_left
tiles.connection: west verge of a roof.

tiles.name: roof_edge_right
tiles.connection: east verge of a roof.

tiles.name: roof_corner_tl
tiles.connection: ridge meeting the west verge.

tiles.name: roof_corner_tr
tiles.connection: ridge meeting the east verge.

tiles.name: roof_corner_bl
tiles.connection: eave meeting the west verge (eave corner transition).

tiles.name: roof_corner_br
tiles.connection: eave meeting the east verge (eave corner transition).

tiles.name: roof_to_facade
tiles.connection: single-tile transition where an eave sits directly on plaster; use INSTEAD of roof_eave + wall_plaster when the building is only one roof row tall.

tiles.name: roof_eave_corner_l
tiles.connection: eave underside wrapping onto a west masonry return.

tiles.name: roof_eave_corner_r
tiles.connection: eave underside wrapping onto an east masonry return.

tiles.name: roof_ridge_end_l
tiles.connection: ridge terminating at a west verge, bond B.

tiles.name: roof_ridge_end_r
tiles.connection: ridge terminating at an east verge, bond B.

tiles.name: threshold
tiles.connection: ground tile placed on the paving directly south of a door. Opaque; replaces the paving tile.

anchor.note: the 23x19 window motif sits at x4..x28, y2..y20 inside the 32x32 field; the rest is plaster_2 so the component drops onto a plaster facade with no halo. On a limestone facade the surrounding plaster must be masked or the component re-exported.

files.layer: architecture, same layer as the facade it replaces
files.notes: shuttered limestone window. Weathered French blue shutters with louvre slats, dark aperture with mullion and transom, lit limestone sill with a recessed underside. Window openings do not imply passability.

anchor.note: place so the lower tile coincides with the plinth row; the component's own base rows (y28-31) are the door's foot, and the separate `threshold` tile goes on the paving row below it.

files.notes: wooden doorway with limestone lintel, framed plank leaf, iron handle. DRAWN AS A COMPONENT ONLY — placement must not imply a traversable route where the engine has none.

suggested_assembly_order: 1. paving — fill the ground with the four cobble variants in any distribution
2. cast shadow — stamp shade_footing on the paving south of the building and shade_corner on the column east of it, offset 2-4px for the north-west light
3. threshold — place on the paving directly south of where the door will go
4. roof ridge row — roof_corner_tl, roof_ridge xN, roof_corner_tr
5. roof plane rows — roof_edge_left, alternating roof_slate_a / roof_slate_b, roof_edge_right
6. roof eave row — roof_corner_bl, roof_eave xN, roof_corner_br
7. facade upper row — wall_edge_left, wall_plaster_course xN, wall_edge_right
8. facade lower row — wall_edge_left, wall_plaster xN, wall_edge_right
9. plinth row — wall_corner_bl, wall_plinth xN, wall_corner_br
10. shade_under_eave overlay on the facade's top row
11. window and door components last, over the facade rows

layering_requirements.ground: cobble and threshold are opaque ground; threshold replaces a paving tile rather than overlaying it
layering_requirements.structural_shadow: indices 13-15 are binary-alpha overlays and must draw ABOVE the ground and BELOW the building and any actor
layering_requirements.components: window and door draw at the same depth as the facade they sit in
layering_requirements.actors: unchanged; characters must still sort above ground and shadow and below nothing in this package

collision.statement: THIS PACKAGE MAKES NO COLLISION CLAIM. No footprint, cover definition, map coordinate or mission value is proposed or implied. Which of these tiles are solid is entirely the coding agent's decision.
collision.art_side_observation: the eave band is part of the building's solid visual footprint per art bible 5.2, but whether it collides is not an art decision
